notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check; the evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. No hardware was attached and no human review or test is claimed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null and the package is model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run wB1-045). The driver is R1 and the loader's refusal of an unreviewed model-written hardware backend applies only at R2 and R3, so at R1 it does not protect this package; a human must review it and sign reviewed_by before any hardware use.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper hint is PythonObjectDriver, but the package uses a direct decorated Driver (the card's decision is direct-driver). The interface needs a per-endpoint stage/group binding chosen after the controller connection, a two-call native stop (abort_group then disable_group), and extension actions with inline output schemas; a config-only family could not express those.

Binding: one stage of one group, selected by the backend options stage and group; with no option the driver takes the first stage the controller reports and the group part of its name. The clone states no physical unit for a position and the travel limits are read from the controller at connection time (newportxps/newportxps.py:250-253), so position is served with the UCUM unit 1 (dimensionless controller user units) and both move inputs are Limit.operator_required. Every move is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the operator supplies the travel range. site-limits.example.json supplies example-only bounds (-1000 to 1000) so the conformance run can exercise the moves; they are not a stage specification and an operator must replace them.

Safety: @estop calls the native abort_group and disable_group on the bound group; the safe state is motion disabled on that group. cap.motion.stop.v1 was not bound because its optional deceleration is in m/s2 and GroupMoveAbort takes no profile. No text of the clone documents an independent hardware e-stop, so estop_physical_ref is not set; R1 does not require SAFE-045. The transport sets a 3600 s socket timeout (newportxps/XPS_C8_drivers.py:94), so a lost network path can still block a native call; a hardware deployment must supervise the link.

NOT COVERED: trajectory definition, arming and running (define_line_trajectories, define_array_trajectory, arm_trajectory, run_trajectory, move_to_trajectory_start, run_line_trajectory_general); gathering reads and files (read_gathering, read_and_save); script and system.ini/stages.ini file operations; tuning and velocity writes (only the tuning dictionary is read); multi-axis group moves (only the single bound stage is moved); FTP upload/download and controller reboot/disconnect-time behaviour beyond the teardown hook; the read_systemini and read_script paths. These are configuration- or file-oriented operations; binding them needs site-specific trajectory files, numeric gain bounds and a larger fake, none of which a text file of the clone states. The position start value, group/stage names, status strings and tuning gains in fake.py are placeholders marked in that file; none was copied into a Fact, a Limit or the reference. The gate reported no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. check-report.json is generated by the gate and is not part of the package.
